coverage_notes: All 51 files in alz1.txt were read in full. Every file captures only the first page of each thread (per file header). Several threads are started by people living with dementia themselves (76429, 76469, 77086, 77330, 77344, 75335 mostly) rather than caregivers; they are tagged cared_for=unclear and kept because they describe diagnosis access and insurance. 64407 is a glossary post with no experiences. 59049 is a 2021 thread that was revived in Oct 2026. Gap lists: all six gap_evidence lists have at least one entry, but entries for paying_for_tools and logins_passwords are thin (few explicit statements). Posters rarely name a single shared tool for the whole family; most mention a notebook, phone calendar, portal, or trackers used by one person.

sources.title: Placement acceptance
sources.problem_one_line: People compare how long a parent, spouse or sibling took to accept a move into memory care and how the caregiver felt afterwards.

sources.title: Common Abbreviations
sources.problem_one_line: Pinned glossary of forum abbreviations (DH, LO, MC, POA, etc.); no personal story.

sources.title: Does It Start Over, And Over, And ....
sources.problem_one_line: Widowed and still-caring spouses describe grief that returns in waves, guilt, and loneliness after the person dies.

sources.title: Anger problems
sources.problem_one_line: One poster asks if anger always comes with dementia; a person with dementia describes a husband who screams at her and a history of credit card debt and bankruptcy.

sources.title: Haven't we all?
sources.problem_one_line: Spouses and a child say they grieved the person for years during caregiving and others do not understand it.

sources.title: Recently diagnosed
sources.problem_one_line: Newly diagnosed people ask whether Medicare and supplements cover the Alzheimer's infusion drugs and compare what they pay; one comment is a commercial herbal clinic ad.

sources.title: Early onset support
sources.problem_one_line: People with early diagnosis struggle to reach memory centers, find a support group that fits work hours, and get infusion drugs covered.
tools_mentioned: list of Centers of Excellence hospitals

sources.title: New Here! Mum diagnosed 6 weeks ago. Struggling with evening sundowning/looping
sources.problem_one_line: Adult child living at home says reassurance, validation and distraction no longer work for mum's evening hallucinations and looping; others suggest medication and UTI checks.

sources.title: Mom's REPETITIVE Calling on Cell Phone
sources.problem_one_line: Mom in care center calls siblings and 911 dozens of times a day; four siblings are split on removing the phone, the phone sits on one sister's plan, and two sisters share POA and disagree.

sources.title: Question from new member
sources.problem_one_line: Adult children living nearby help mom caregive for dad; his confabulated stories about a past affair devastate mom and they lack information.
tools_mentioned: links and PDFs shared by members

sources.title: Newly Diagnosed MCI with underlying Alzheimer's Pathology
sources.problem_one_line: Newly diagnosed people wait weeks to months for neurologist evaluation; a spouse shares persistence tactics and advice to keep copies of records.

sources.title: Eating
sources.problem_one_line: Wife forgets she has eaten or had wine and keeps eating and drinking; members suggest hiding food and single servings.

sources.title: the in between stages
sources.problem_one_line: Daughter whose mother lives with her wonders if a lost-walker needs a caregiver or a GPS watch; others debate whether a tracker is enough.

sources.title: Gotta see the humor
sources.problem_one_line: Members swap funny moments with a spouse or parent with dementia; one spouse says she cannot leave him with others even for a few hours.

sources.title: Elder sibling recently Dx'd; I'm struggling with coordination of relevant professionals
sources.problem_one_line: Sister living an hour away is the only support for her older sibling and cannot find one source to sort finances, assisted living cost and legal papers while the other brother is rarely involved.

sources.title: Nothing To Do
sources.problem_one_line: Spouses say keeping a wife or husband with advanced dementia occupied all day is exhausting even with adult day care.

sources.title: Reducing sensory overload
sources.problem_one_line: Caregivers compare how sounds, TV, textures and food overwhelm the person and how hard each stimulus is to track.

sources.title: Testing for memory loss
sources.problem_one_line: Spouses react to falling cognitive test scores and the doctor stopping annual testing; one feels solely responsible.

sources.title: Gentle corrections
sources.problem_one_line: Partner asks whether to point out or quietly fix task errors; members mostly say let it go and fix in secret.

sources.title: Vascular Dementia horrible dreaming

sources.title: Hallucination Distractions

sources.title: Overwhelmed
sources.problem_one_line: Adult child cannot sleep from fear of losing dad, who has Alzheimer's and now bladder cancer.

sources.title: Young onset of Dementia

sources.title: Hospice time

sources.title: Anger

sources.title: Closing eyes

sources.title: New to all of this and scared

sources.problem_one_line: Spouse needs a compact home blood-pressure device whose readings can go to several doctors; the cardiology office gave no specific advice.

sources.title: Suggestions for parents running out of money?
sources.problem_one_line: Adult child managing two divorced parents' finances faces savings running out in two years and asks how Medicaid, lookback and facility acceptance work.

sources.title: Family Expectations
sources.problem_one_line: Wife in the care role is criticized by her husband's sister over his clothes in memory care.

sources.title: The Time Has Come...
sources.problem_one_line: Wife with her own illnesses is moving her husband into memory care; members say caregiving continues and advise noting concerns for staff meetings.

sources.title: Getting someone to help
sources.problem_one_line: Husband wants someone to stay with his wife but expects her to be upset; members suggest framing as a club or helper for him.

sources.title: DW with VD, repetitious questions and stories
sources.problem_one_line: Caregivers cope with the same question many times a day; tactics include answer-and-redirect, a pad, calendar or message board.

sources.title: more ugliness to come
sources.problem_one_line: Wife's moods switch suddenly with constant criticism; members advise a symptom notebook, a private note to the doctor and a behavioral assessment tool.

sources.title: New to the group (unfortunately)
sources.problem_one_line: Husband of a 53-year-old with new Alzheimer's diagnosis sees fire risk, online shopping and driving issues while raising three daughters; members list legal, financial and safety steps.

sources.title: GPS tracking devices
sources.problem_one_line: Wife wants a better tracker than FindMy for a husband who likes to walk; members list TILE, AirTag and Project Lifesaver.

sources.title: Inpatient evaluation - thoughts?
sources.problem_one_line: Husband of a woman in hospice has seen many sedatives and antipsychotics and doubts an inpatient evaluation; others warn about drug cocktails and switching.

sources.title: Fall Prevention
sources.problem_one_line: Daughter's mother in a wheelchair keeps trying to stand and falls; members discuss seat alarms and restraint rules at home versus facility.

sources.title: New to This
sources.problem_one_line: Wife working full time with no family nearby receives a long to-do checklist (lawyer, HIPAA, passwords, trackers, day care, waitlists).

sources.title: RIP Dad
sources.problem_one_line: Daughter says dad's dementia was missed by doctors and she and sisters kept their distance; he bounced between ER, hospital and psych ward.

sources.title: Moving Mom Soon, but how?
sources.problem_one_line: Student son acts as mom's assistant, scheduler and IT tech, is unsure how much to involve her in choosing assisted living, and an older brother is not involved.

sources.title: Move now or later
sources.problem_one_line: Wife in a remote home with a newly diagnosed husband asks whether to move now; replies cover driving, home maintenance, selling and anesthesia during knee surgery.

sources.title: Time for Memory Care
sources.problem_one_line: Working wife wants advice on telling husband about memory care and what to do with his phone; replies cover cost, Medicaid lookback and lorazepam after placement.

sources.title: My Dad is 64 with Moderate Alzheimer's

sources.problem_one_line: Son caring for mother with Alzheimer's and leukemia needs money-saving help to repair her house before sale to fund care.

new_themes.name: Caregiving continues after placement
new_themes.description: Spouses and children say moving the person to memory care does not end the work: they advocate with staff, track concerns, manage the phone, handle medication changes by phone.

example.quote: Memory care is a new turn on the journey, and the caregiving does not end when you LO is placed.

new_themes.name: Therapeutic fibs as a management tool
new_themes.description: Caregivers describe telling made-up reasons (rehab, doctor's orders, phone being fixed) to get through placement, phone removal and moves.

example.quote: Therapeutic lies, aka "fiblets", are how most caregivers manage to make the changes they need to make to keep their LO safe.

new_themes.name: Keeping the person occupied all day
new_themes.description: Spouses with advanced dementia say the constant job of entertaining and engaging their person is a separate exhausting load beyond bathing and feeding.

example.quote: The entertainment and engagement effort is exhausting to me.

new_themes.name: Partner versus caregiver identity
new_themes.description: Spouses describe losing the role of husband or wife and turning into nurse or caregiver, with both relief and grief.

example.quote: I started thinking of my husband as my patient, not my spouse.

new_themes.name: Finding support and information alone
new_themes.description: Newly diagnosed people and caregivers say they must research on their own, support groups are full or meet only in daytime, and they rely on pasted lists and PDFs from other members.

example.quote: Sadly you have to do just as your doing, a lot of research on your own to find support groups.

new_themes.name: Commercial or spam replies in the forum
new_themes.description: At least two replies in these threads are promotional (herbal clinic, assisted living ad).

caveats: ALZConnected is a self-selected Alzheimer's Association forum; most posters care for a spouse or are people with dementia themselves, so parent-caregiver and sibling-coordination material is thinner than in a general caregiver sample. Only the first page of each thread was captured. Theme assignment is one primary per thread based on my reading; threads often span several themes. Tool and cost mentions are what posters named, not a survey. Quote locators use the POST/COMMENT n labels from the files. Replies with only a link, empty comments, or deleted-user notes were ignored. Several threads are people with dementia speaking for themselves (76429, 76469, 77086, 77330, 77344, parts of 75335), tagged cared_for=unclear.
